# AQI Tower: what we are building next

Working name; final project name is still to be selected.

We want to build a tower that draws air through filters and returns cleaner air. The long-term idea is several outdoor towers creating useful local cleaner-air zones. We do not yet know how large those zones can be, or whether a chain will work well in real wind.

## Work completed

We have made computer models, compared airflow shapes, studied a real fan and HEPA filter candidate, and identified a filter bypass problem. A sealed computer case predicted about 1,332 m3/h, but the calculation was not fully converged and has not been physically verified. We evaluated and removed the water-spray stage from the current plan. The earlier small-device work was digital only.

## What happens now

We will prepare actual assembly drawings and safe electrical plans, build one full-size filter/fan prototype, and test it indoors. This lets us check airflow, filter sealing, power, noise and particle cleaning in a controlled space. After that, a separately reviewed outdoor prototype will be tested before promising an area or adding multiple towers.

## Support needed

College and NGO: funding support only, as clarified by the team. No college lab, workshop, instruments or reviewer is assumed. Funding must cover components, fabrication, equipment purchase/rental, qualified review and testing services. The college PBL can document drawings, calculations, an assembled test unit and an honest evidence report when achieved.

The team must separately secure a test space and future pilot permission; NGO site assistance is not assumed. An ENTC engineer may check the assistant-prepared work, but participation is unconfirmed and not a delivery dependency. Present status transparently; academic and NGO funding routes do not change safety or performance limitations.

Funding request comes after exact parts and fabrication quotes. We will buy standard parts where sensible, fabricate the metal structure locally, and avoid unnecessary electronics and solar purchases during the first test.

## What we cannot claim yet

No proven outdoor bubble size, cleaning percentage, gas-removal performance, certified whole-device HEPA performance, or finished physical prototype. The next milestone is a safely assembled unit with repeatable indoor measurements—not a city-scale pollution solution.
